subject: Concierge onboarding subsidy and contract carveout request
messages:
From: Maya Shah <maya@brighttune.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brighttune.com, Sam Reed <sam.reed@brighttune.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring replacement economics + onboarding assistance

Jordan —

Thanks for taking the time on the call yesterday. BrightTune is evaluating a vendor replacement to consolidate inference spend and simplify runtime ops. Two quick asks from procurement/engineering before we scope an internal recommendation:

1) Can Redwood provide a short paper outlining a migration credit structure you’d offer for a 12-month commitment that includes a dedicated onboarding concierge (hands-on SRE support, up to 80 hours)?

2) We have an existing termination carveout in our current contract that limits liability for certain egress/ingress during cutover. Can you outline how Redwood would handle a limited carveout or transition subsidy?

High level numbers: current run-rate ~ $180k/month, peak tokens in bursts, and nontrivial KV cache needs. We’re sensitive to both unit economics and go-live risk.

If you can get a starter proposal by early next week that covers credits, packaging constraints (seats vs runtime units), and a simple implementation scope, that’ll help our procurement timeline.

Best,
Maya
Procurement Lead | BrightTune

---
Attachment: current_vendor_term_summary.pdf (stub)

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Maya Shah <maya@brighttune.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2025 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement economics + onboarding assistance

Maya —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can definitely put together a concise proposal. To set expectations up front: our standard approach for migration economics combines a time-limited onboarding subsidy (credits applied against invoice) and an optional concierge engagement (SRE hours billed from a dedicated credit bucket). Typically we separate:

- Onboarding subsidy: up-front credit equal to X months of committed usage, drawn down over the first 60–90 days.
- Concierge hours: pool of SRE hours (80 in your ask) delivered by our onboarding team; can be consumed for runbook creation, KV/cache tuning, and handoffs.
- Carveouts: we can offer a transitional carveout defined as a capped egress/ingress reimbursement for documented cutover traffic for up to 30 days.

Before I model numbers: can you confirm expected committed MRR you’d feel comfortable contracting to (even a range), and whether BrightTune needs seat-based licensing (per-seat admin) or purely runtime billing? That changes how credits amortize.

I’ll draft a short proposal and send an initial credit schedule + simple scope doc Monday. Looping in Lauren (sales lead) and Connor (commercial ops) to align on approvals.

—Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachment: redwood_concierge_credit_schedule.pdf (pro forma stub)

From: Sam Reed <sam.reed@brighttune.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: Maya Shah <maya@brighttune.com>, procurement@brighttune.com
Date: Mon, 21 Apr 2025 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement economics + onboarding assistance

Jordan —

Thanks. For modeling please assume a committed baseline of $120k/month (we may stretch to $150k.MONTH after pilot). On licensing: we prefer runtime-only (no seat fees) but will accept up to 5 admin seats as part of the bundle.

Also, two engineering notes: 
- We’ll want a KV warming plan (warm the cache before cutover) and an ability to burst to 2x baseline QPS for short windows during launch.
- Security needs: SOC 2 evidence and an audit log export for the first 90 days post-migration.

If you can bake those in and show net delta vs our current vendor (we’ll share the vendor runbook offline), we can accelerate.

—Sam

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Apr 2025 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: draft concession math for BrightTune

Jordan / Lauren —

I sketched three concession packages (attached) that meet the asks. High level:

1) Quick Pilot Bundle — 3 months onboarding credit = 30% of committed MRR, 40 SRE hours concierge, limited carveout up to $25k. Good for fast pilots, smaller net NPV hit.

2) Standard Migration Pack — 6 months onboarding credit = 50% of committed MRR, 80 SRE hours concierge (dedicated), carveout up to $60k, SOC 2 evidence + 90-day audit logs included. Best balance.

3) Enterprise Assurance — 9 months onboarding credit = 75% of committed MRR, 120 SRE hours, carveout up to $150k, dedicated escalation SLA and one-week white-glove runbook handoff.

Notes on amortization: for runtime-only customers we apply credits as a dollar offset against monthly usage until exhausted; for seat-included bundles we prorate credits across seats and runtime. For BrightTune’s $120k baseline I’ve modeled Quick/Standard/Enterprise NPV and cashflow.

Two tricky points to pre-check: carveout cap and whether procurement wants the carveout to be a credit or direct reimbursement. Direct reimbursement increases complexity for finance.

See attached: onboard_scope-statement.docx and concession_math.xlsx (stubs).

—Connor O’Brien
Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Maya Shah <maya@brighttune.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: Sam Reed <sam.reed@brighttune.com>, procurement@brighttune.com
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement economics + onboarding assistance

Connor / Jordan —

Helpful breakdown — thank you. A few follow-ups from procurement/eng: 

- The carveout as a credit is preferred (simpler on our side). Can you show what the Standard Migration Pack looks like if the $60k carveout is a credit applied against month 1–3 vs applied only as a reimbursement?
- For the SOC 2 evidence and audit logs: will that be part of a standard evidence bundle or require a separate professional services engagement?
- We’d like the 80 SRE hours to be split: 40 hours pre-cutover (runbook/warm), 40 hours post-cutover hypercare. Can you commit to that split in SOW language?

If you can update the short proposal with those clarifications we’ll review and aim to put a PO in the queue the week after next.

Best —
Maya

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Maya Shah <maya@brighttune.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Apr 2025 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement economics + onboarding assistance

Maya —

Thanks — attached is an updated one-pager that shows Standard Migration Pack variations with carveout as an upfront credit vs reimbursement and the SRE hour split asked for. Key commitments:

- Carveout as credit: applied as a line-item credit across the first 3 invoices until exhausted (clean for your finance team).
- SOC 2 & audit logs: SOC 2 evidence is available as part of our standard compliance bundle; audit log exports for 90 days are included in the Standard Migration Pack (no extra PS required).
- SRE split: we’ll codify 40/40 pre/post in the SOW and assign a named onboarding lead.

Next steps: if BrightTune confirms the Standard Migration Pack with $120k baseline, I’ll prepare a term sheet and draft SOW + send to DocuSign. Proposed PO window: week of May 5.

If that timeline works I’ll also ask Finance to prepare a phased credit schedule so accounting has the invoice examples.

—Jordan
